subject.title: [RFC] Multi-Session Architecture: Shared LLM + Isolated Sessions + Public Knowledge Base

question: Should #48874 remain the umbrella RFC for multi-session architecture, or should maintainers close/supersede it in favor of narrower product-approved trackers?
rationale: The request changes core routing, storage, UI, config, and privacy policy, so automation cannot choose the permanent architecture or security boundary safely.

options.title: Keep as umbrella and split work
options.body: Use #48874 for architecture coordination while moving accepted slices into narrower session-family, channel-routing, UI lifecycle, and shared-memory/security issues.

options.title: Supersede with narrower canonicals
options.body: Close this RFC after pointing users to active narrower issues such as topic-session families and Google Chat routing where the remaining work can be reviewed independently.

options.title: Reject the broad core architecture
options.body: Close the umbrella as too broad for core and require optional capability to live in plugins or separate designs unless a missing core API is proven.

recommendation.title: Keep as umbrella and split work
recommendation.body: Use #48874 for architecture coordination while moving accepted slices into narrower session-family, channel-routing, UI lifecycle, and shared-memory/security issues.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work on session grouping and lifecycle touched the central protocol, gateway, config, and UI surfaces implicated by the RFC.
